objects.taxonomy_description: Adult male bird exhibiting pronounced sexual dimorphism from female. Body is compact and robust measuring 30-70 cm in length depending on species. Plumage is characterized by vivid, iridescent coloration with metallic green, blue, purple, or copper tones on the neck, breast, and tail feathers. Hackle feathers (neck plumage) are elongated, pointed, and glossy, forming a distinctive ruff around the neck. Saddle feathers (lower back) are elongated and flowing. Tail feathers are long, curved, and iridescent with a characteristic arching posture. Comb is a fleshy, serrated crest on the crown, bright red and vascularized; size and shape vary by breed. Wattles are paired fleshy appendages hanging from the lower beak, also bright red. Beak is short, curved, and keratinous with a yellow to grey coloration. Legs are stout with thick, scaled skin and a prominent posterior spur (calcified projection) on the tarsus used in combat. Feet are anisodactyl (three toes forward, one backward) with sharp, curved claws. The bird exhibits an upright, alert posture with chest puffed and tail elevated.

objects.taxonomy_description: Composite flower with a central yellow disc surrounded by a single whorl of white ray petals (florets). The flower head measures 2-5 cm in diameter with 13-34 elongated white petals radiating outward from the bright yellow center. The petals are narrow, slightly pointed, and arranged in a flat, circular pattern. The flower is supported by a slender green stem with small alternate leaves. The center disc has a bumpy, granular texture from individual disc florets.

objects.taxonomy_description: Medium-sized freshwater to brackish water turtle measuring 12-25 cm in carapace length. Carapace is oval and moderately domed with a smooth surface; coloration varies from brown to olive with concentric growth rings visible on each scute. Some species exhibit ornate patterning with yellow or orange markings on dark scutes. Plastron is large and hinged, enabling partial closure. Head is moderately sized with a pointed snout and small eyes; skin coloration is grey to olive with distinctive striped or spotted patterning on the head and neck. Limbs are moderately long with webbed feet and sharp claws. Tail is short. The turtle exhibits a characteristic basking posture on logs or banks with limbs extended and head raised. Skin texture is smooth with fine scales. Adapted for both aquatic and terrestrial environments, spending significant time basking to regulate body temperature.
